subject: Account wiring + ops clearance for Private Deployment
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@starlitehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evan Miles <evan.miles@starlitehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Account wiring + ops clearance for Private Deployment

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Starlite is ready to move forward with the private deployment (VPC) for our inference workloads, and we want to lock in the account wiring steps and a short ops clearance checklist so our network team can start scheduling. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirmation of required service accounts and a contact for day-0 SSH/jumpbox access
- A minimal list of ports/IPs for egress and health checks we must allow
- Any KMS/HSM key naming conventions or KMS integration window notes

I attached our internal kickoff note for context. Can your team confirm whether we should send network evidence to an email inbox or upload to the Drive link? Evan (cc) will coordinate the IT side.

Goal: have the mutual action plan and a basic network evidence bucket ready by next Wednesday so we can schedule engineering access the following week.

Cheers,
Jordan Price
Head of Platform Integrations
Starlite Health

Attachment: starlite-kickoff-notes.docx (referenced)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@starlitehealth.com>
Cc: Evan Miles <evan.miles@starlitehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Account wiring + ops clearance for Private Deployment

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and the call earlier.

Short answers up-front: Drive upload is preferred for evidence, we require one service account per environment (staging/prod), and we use a short-lived bastion for day-0 access (we'll provide jump credentials and a time window). See the attached Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft — I dropped a timeline and ownership columns.

Action items for Starlite (what we need from you):
1) Network evidence folder: public IPs for NAT/egress, firewall allowlist entries, and current ACL snapshots.
2) KMS owner + key alias you want Redwood to use for envelope encryption. If you require customer-managed keys in your KMS, indicate whether it's Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS.
3) Point person for procurement to sign the reserved capacity addendum (if you choose Dedicated later).

Ben — looping you for the network egress specifics and the smoke-test port list. Kimberly — tagging you for KMS and compliance notes (SOC 2 evidence flow).

I attached: starlite-mutual-action-plan-v1.xlsx and a network-evidence-template.pdf to speed the upload. Upload to the Drive link in this thread and drop a quick note when done.

Proposed dates: evidence uploaded by 2028-07-27, day-0 access window 2028-08-03 to 2028-08-04. If that works, we'll lock calendar invites.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: starlite-mutual-action-plan-v1.xlsx, network-evidence-template.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@starlitehealth.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kim Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Account wiring + ops clearance for Private Deployment

Jordan / Aisha — quick notes from the infra side:

Network egress & smoke test checklist (minimal):
- Allow outbound to ecr.redwoodinfra.example.com (443) for container pulls
- Allow outbound to auth.redwoodinfra.example.com (443) for token exchange
- Health-check ping endpoints: 10.0.12.0/24 (internal), we will provide signed URLs for readiness checks
- Port 22: SSH only to bastion public IP during scheduled windows (we will provide ephemeral credentials)
- TLS enforced for all egress; no plaintext endpoints

Bastion/jumpbox details:
- We'll provide a one-time signed SSH cert with 4-hour validity for day-0 access. Please ensure your jump host admin can accept cert-based SSH and that their jumpbox clock is NTP synced.

Notes on MTU/Peering: if you plan to peer directly to our VPC, confirm MTU settings (we prefer 1500) and whether you require static routes vs. BGP — provide your network owner's preference in the Drive doc.

I'll post a short tech checklist to the Drive template now. Sean will be your ops on-call during the handoff.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Technical Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Miles <evan.miles@starlitehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@starlitehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Jul 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Account wiring + ops clearance for Private Deployment

Thanks — confirms the plan from Starlite side. A few clarifying points from our network team after reviewing Ben's checklist:

- We'll upload the NAT IP ranges and firewall exports to the Drive by COB Monday (2028-07-24).
- We run Azure Key Vault for KMS; will add the key alias and the subscription/tenant id in the MAP. Is there a Redwood support window for key rotation metadata?
- For peering we prefer BGP; I will note our ASN and desired prefixes in the Drive template.

One ask: can Redwood provide the specific FQDNs your runtime uses for telemetry and metrics ingestion so we can allow them explicitly? That would reduce our egress footprint.

Jordan and I will get the Drive upload done Monday. Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to locking dates.

Best,
Evan Miles
IT Infrastructure, Starlite Health
